sections.heading: Solving basic trigonometric equations on the unit circle

questions.q: Find all solutions to $\sin\theta = -\frac{1}{2}$ in the interval $[0, 2\pi)$.
questions.answer: Reference angle $\frac{\pi}{6}$, sine negative in QIII and QIV: $\theta = \frac{7\pi}{6}, \frac{11\pi}{6}$.

questions.q: Find all solutions to $2\cos\theta + \sqrt{3} = 0$ in the interval $[0, 2\pi)$.
questions.answer: $\cos\theta = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$: reference angle $\frac{\pi}{6}$, cosine negative in QII and QIII: $\theta = \frac{5\pi}{6}, \frac{7\pi}{6}$.

sections.heading: Building the unit circle from special triangles

questions.q: Using the $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle, derive the exact coordinates of the point on the unit circle at $\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$.
questions.answer: A $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle with hypotenuse $1$ has legs $\frac{1}{2}$ and $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. At $\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$ ($60°$), $x=\cos\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{1}{2}$, $y=\sin\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. Point: $\left(\frac{1}{2},\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$.

questions.q: State the coordinates of all four points on the unit circle where the terminal side lies along an axis ($\theta=0,\frac{\pi}{2},\pi,\frac{3\pi}{2}$).

sections.heading: Using the Pythagorean identity with unit circle points

questions.q: A point on the unit circle has $x$-coordinate $\frac{7}{25}$ and lies in Quadrant IV. Find its $y$-coordinate using $x^2+y^2=1$.
Given $\sin\theta=0.6$ and $\theta$ in Quadrant II, find $\cos\theta$ and $\tan\theta$ exactly (using the fact $0.6=\frac{3}{5}$).
The unit circle $x^2+y^2=1$ is shown. Use it to estimate $\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)$ and $\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)$ visually, then state the exact values.
questions.answer: The angle $\frac{2\pi}{3}$ ($120°$) lies in QII, roughly two-thirds around from $0$. Exact values: $\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}=-\frac{1}{2}$, $\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

sections.heading: Solving for the angle given exact coordinates

questions.q: Find all values of $\theta$ in $[0,2\pi)$ for which the unit circle point is exactly $\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)$.
questions.answer: This point lies in QIII where both coordinates are negative with reference angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$: $\theta=\pi+\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{5\pi}{4}$ (only one solution in $[0,2\pi)$ since the exact point pins down a single angle).
